checks.why: control (#1556): a lambda written inside one test serves that test and not a sibling, with the C# helper rule narrowed
control: a direct call from one test names that test only
a helper of the test class serves the test that calls it, on that test's own resolved route
near-miss control: a helper of the test class that no test calls or names is credited to no test
xUnit builds an IClassFixture<T> before the tests of the class that names it: T's constructor serves them (#1498)
near-miss control: a fixture class no test class names reaches no test (#1498)
an override of a class fixture's framework base (a WebApplicationFactory's ConfigureWebHost) runs for every test of the class that names the fixture, though nothing in the graph calls it (#1498)
near-miss control: a member of the class fixture that a test calls is carried by that call, to that test only
a collection fixture serves the tests of each class in the [Collection] its [CollectionDefinition] names
a test class's Dispose runs after each of its tests, so what it reaches is credited to every test of that class
a [MemberData] source on another type (MemberType = typeof(...)) serves the test that names it (#1499)
a [MemberData] source on the test's own class serves the test that names it, not every test of the class (#1499)
